suite_notes: The ANSWER half of the analytics gate: the verbatim question text the chat-path gate runner sends, one entry per section of ground-truth/EXPECTED.md. This file is the only place a gate question is defined — scripts/analytics_gate_run.py reads it and records its git blob sha in the run document, so a score is reproducible and a reworded question shows up as a diff instead of as a regression. Do NOT confuse it with ../tool-selection/analytics-gate.json, which scores which TOOLS get selected for a similar-looking utterance and carries ids in the same qNN space; the cross-link is tool_selection_fixture_id on each entry.

chat_path_gate.rationale: Every question whose serving endpoints have shipped (Wave 1 and Wave 2, analytics-capability-plan.md §3/§4) AND whose ground truth is computable on the TRACKB seed AND whose Wave 2 call count is inside its §6 budget. The other eight are excluded for a stated reason on their own entry — an unbuilt Wave 3 composition, an over-budget Wave 2 loop, or a BLOCKED ground truth. The set is the Wave 2 exit gate (docs/gate-runs/wave-2/README.md) plus Wave 1's q13.

window_shapes.calendar: Whole calendar periods ending with the last COMPLETE one (SystemPromptDefaults window rules, #1661/#1670).
window_shapes.rolling: The period ending on the as-of date.
window_shapes.point-in-time: A balance or state measured at the as-of instant; no range.
window_shapes.mixed: Two independent conditions in one question that keep different shapes.

questions.utterance: Who were our top technicians by labor revenue last month, and what was their average billed hours per completed work order?
Compare each technician's completed work orders, billed hours and labor revenue over the last three months.
questions.excluded_reason: Wave 3 `technicianPerformance` composition (plan §W3.2) is not built; the Wave 2 early-pass path is a 3 x E5 loop above the §6 budget of 2.

window.notes: QUESTION/GROUND-TRUTH GAP. `over the last three months` reads ROLLING under the #1670 preposition rule, but the ground truth buckets the three complete calendar months Jun/Jul/Aug 2026. Excluded from the gate today, so the gap is inert; restate to `in the last three months` before promoting this question.

questions.utterance: Which technicians had the most work orders reopened within seven days of completion this quarter?

window.notes: Boundary-day divergence only. `this quarter` resolves to 2026-07-01..2026-08-31 under the calendar rule (whole periods ending with the last complete month); the ground truth runs to the as-of date 2026-09-01 inclusive. Inert on the TRACKB seed — no reopen pair falls on 2026-09-01 — and the 2026-09-03 run PASSed under both readings.

questions.utterance: What was the average time from work order creation to invoice, by month, for the last six months?

expected_plan.per: one getInvoicingLag call per month, single-window E4 has no groupBy (plan §6 row 4)

questions.utterance: Which customers are more than 60 days past due, and what open work orders do we currently have for them?

window.notes: `past due` and `currently` are both measured at the as-of date; aging is by due date since #1604.

expected_plan.per: one searchWorkorders call per past-due customer (#1676 status=OPEN, one call per customer id)

questions.utterance: Show me revenue, parts cost, labor cost and gross margin by customer for last month.
questions.excluded_reason: Ground truth is BLOCKED. E13 customer-margin is deferred to Wave 3 by decision D2 (plan §W2.4) and parts cost is unseeded and unseedable until D2's cost-sourcing decision lands, so there is no expected margin to score against.

questions.utterance: Who were our top customers by revenue over the last twelve months compared with the twelve months before that?

window.notes: QUESTION/GROUND-TRUTH GAP. `over the last twelve months` reads ROLLING, and the comparison phrase `the twelve months before that` names no calendar period, so the #1670 mixed-comparison precedence does not fire and both windows read rolling — while the ground truth measures both on the calendar. With EVAL_AS_OF on a month boundary the two readings differ only at the endpoints, so the gap has not yet moved a score (q07 DEFLECTed on 2026-09-03). Resolve by restating to `in the last twelve months compared with the twelve months before that` when the question is next revised.

questions.utterance: Which customers have not bought anything in the last 90 days but spent more than $10,000 with us in the prior year?

window.resolved_range: no invoice on or after 2026-06-03 (rolling 90 days); revenue in 2024-09-01..2025-08-31 (calendar prior year)
window.notes: Two independent conditions, not a comparison: a day-expressed range is always rolling (#1670), and `the prior year` is calendar. The paired-window rule deliberately does not apply here.

questions.utterance: For our top 20 customers by revenue in the last twelve months, show revenue, invoice count, average invoice value, outstanding balance and average days to pay.

window.resolved_range: revenue, count, average and days-to-pay over 2025-09-01..2026-08-31; outstanding balance as of 2026-09-01
window.notes: #1671 fix. The previous wording carried NO window, while EXPECTED.md Q9 and the ground-truth SQL both measure the twelve calendar months ending 2026-08-31 — which is what made the 2026-09-03 answer UNSCORABLE. `in the last twelve months` resolves to exactly that range under the #1670 calendar rule. The outstanding balance stays a point-in-time figure at the as-of date, as the ground truth computes it.

expected_plan.per: E1 revenue-by-customer ranking plus one aging call for outstanding balance/days-to-pay (plan §6 row 9)

questions.utterance: Which customers have rising sales but also rising past-due balances over the last three months?
questions.excluded_reason: The past-due trend half has no computable ground truth: generateAgedReceivables applies each invoice's CURRENT open balance to a historical asOfDate, so a month-end A/R series is not a point-in-time balance. EXPECTED.md Q10 records the trend half as BLOCKED pending W3.1 point-in-time replay.

window.resolved_range: 2026-06-01..2026-08-31, bucketed by month; aging as of each month-end
window.notes: Same preposition gap as q02: `over the last three months` reads rolling, the ground truth buckets calendar months. Inert while the question is excluded.

questions.utterance: How much did we invoice versus collect each week for the last twelve weeks, and what is the collection rate?
questions.excluded_reason: The Wave 2 path is a 12 x E2 loop, at the §6 budget edge of 13 and so unable to demonstrate criterion 3 (bounded cost); the intended single-call path is W3.1 `groupBy=week`, which is not built.

window.notes: EXPECTED.md Q11 answers the settlement question (settled / invoiced) and also reports the cash-only collection rate, per the #1605 money-measure split; both must be labelled in the answer.

questions.utterance: Of the invoices we issued in the last six months, how many were paid within 30 days, 31 to 60 days, 61 to 90 days, or are still unpaid?

window.notes: `in the last six months` is the calendar form under the #1670 preposition rule. The 2026-09-03 run answered it on a rolling 2026-03-04..2026-09-03 window and was scored FAIL; that is the model behaviour #1670 addresses, not a question defect.

questions.utterance: Which customers make up most of our accounts receivable balance, and how much of each is past due?
What was our accounts receivable balance and DSO at each month-end for the last 12 months?
questions.excluded_reason: Formally withdrawn at Wave 1 (plan §3) and Wave 3 thereafter: a true A/R balance trend needs the point-in-time balance reconstruction W3.1 has not delivered. EXPECTED.md Q14 scores only the latest as-of point; the other eleven are BLOCKED.

questions.utterance: Who were our largest vendors by spend over the last six months compared with the same six months last year?

window.notes: Resolved by the #1670 mixed-comparison precedence: `over the last six months` alone reads rolling, but it is paired with `the same six months last year`, which names a specific period, so BOTH windows take the calendar shape — matching the ground truth.

expected_plan.per: two getVendorSpend windows, current and same-period-last-year (plan §6 row 15)

questions.utterance: Which vendor bills are due in the next 14 days, and how much cash do we need each day to cover them?

window.resolved_range: due 2026-09-01..2026-09-15 (14 days inclusive, forward from the as-of)
window.notes: A day-expressed range has no calendar form (#1670) — forward-rolling from the as-of date.

questions.utterance: Which vendors have increased their average bill amount by more than 10% year over year?

window.notes: OPEN QUESTION/GROUND-TRUTH GAP — the same defect class #1671 fixed on q09, left open deliberately. The question names no window at all; `year over year` says only that two equal periods are compared. The ground truth inherits q15's six-month windows because both are served by the same E8 call, which is an implementation accident, not something the question says. Any score on q17 is therefore conditional on the grader accepting those windows. Fixing it means either restating the question with an explicit period or restating EXPECTED.md Q17 against a twelve-month year-over-year comparison; that choice interacts with the q15/q17 reading corrected by #1670 and is tracked separately.

expected_plan.per: two getVendorSpend windows, current and same-period-last-year, compared on avgIssuedBillAmount (plan §6 row 17)

questions.utterance: Show weekly cash in versus cash out for the last quarter and flag any week where we were cash negative.
questions.excluded_reason: The Wave 2 path costs 27 calls against a §6 budget of 3, so plan §6 reclassifies it as a Wave 3 gate pending the E2 + A/P weekly groupBy.

window.notes: QUESTION/GROUND-TRUTH GAP. `the last quarter` reads as the last complete calendar quarter (2026-04-01..2026-06-30) under the #1670 rule, but the ground truth measures the thirteen weeks ending 2026-08-30 so the weekly buckets stay whole. Inert while the question is excluded; restate to `the last thirteen weeks` before promoting it.
